title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: policy alert improvements
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the roadmap target from Microsoft's later rollout notice and correctly reports the feature as available by default. Its licensing, existing alert controls and notification baseline are supported; the behaviour of existing policies under the new settings remains explicitly unconfirmed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate additional licence requirement for the alert improvements is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "alert improvements" licensing pricing; read MC920304, learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure and the Microsoft Purview service description. Product subscriptions are documented; no alert-improvement-specific entitlement was found.

claims.claim: Administrators must verify that the organization has a supported subscription.
claims.quote: To access and use Communication Compliance, administrators need to verify that their organization has a supported subscription and that users have the appropriate licenses assigned.

claims.claim: Users must have appropriate licences assigned, with details linked from the getting-started page.
claims.quote: users have the appropriate licenses assigned. For more information about subscriptions and licensing, see the subscription requirements for Communication Compliance.

claims.claim: Detecting inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data requires enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Additionally, to detect inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, you need to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: Detecting inappropriate or risky interactions for Microsoft 365 Copilot data has no pay-as-you-go requirements or charges.
claims.quote: There aren't any pay-as-you-go billing requirements or charges for Microsoft 365 detecting inappropriate or risky interaction for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Alert policies page in Microsoft Purview lets administrators change activity-count, period and specific-user alert triggers.
claims.quote: You can change the default settings for triggers on number of activities, period for the activities, and for specific users in alert policies on the Alert policies page in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: No automation operation for configuring these Communication Compliance alert triggers is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance alert policies Set-ProtectionAlert PowerShell threshold timewindow; "Communication Compliance" "API" "alert" settings; Microsoft Graph API settings. Read policies and Set-ProtectionAlert: the latter only edits alerts created with New-ProtectionAlert, not default policies.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide UI or API switch for the new alert-frequency and recipient settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance new alerts page alert frequency recipients disable tenant settings; "Communication Compliance" "alert" "disable" "tenant"; Microsoft Graph API settings. Read MC920304, policies and configure; no tenant-wide switch for these improvements was found.

claims.claim: The documented existing alert-trigger control is not identified as replaced by the new wizard page.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance new alerts page alert frequency recipients policy tenant switch PowerShell API alert policies. Read MC920304 and learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-policies; neither states that the new wizard page replaces the existing alert-trigger control.

claims.claim: The documented minimum activity threshold for Communication Compliance alert policies is three.
claims.quote: The alert policy threshold trigger settings for activities support a minimum value of 3 or higher for Communication Compliance policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn says PowerShell is not supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies.
claims.quote: PowerShell isn't supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies. To create and manage these policies, use the policy management controls in the Communication Compliance solution.

controlChecks.governs: Alert policy triggers for a Communication Compliance policy: number of activities, period and specific users
